topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks establish the lecture's objectives, historical context, and key themes in cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of transforming genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed that cancer arises from altered cellular genes and established laboratory assays for cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer-associated mutations are defined and how they disrupt cellular regulation through pathway control and differing allele dosage effects.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures in distinct DNA repair pathways and mitotic processes generate sequence and chromosomal instability, driving cellular stress and adaptation.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the stepwise accumulation of mutations and inherited predispositions accelerate tumor progression and determine clinical cancer phenotypes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks conclude the presentation, suggest follow-up reading, and preview the next lecture.
